summary.name: Editorial Design, in the Graphic Design and Design Movements category. The source explicitly describes this visual direction.
summary.visualIdentity: Magazine or book reading logic organizes headlines, short copy, images and annotations on one consistent grid. Serif-sans-serif pairings are purposeful. Information reveals in reading order, with transitions through cropping, grouped movement or layout changes, not whole-page slides.
summary.suitableUses: Explicit: article-like narratives with images and pull quotes, plus listed good fits for UI and product storytelling, editorial and minimalist layouts, and staged geometric motion posters. Source best-fit examples include feature stories, case studies and behind-the-scenes explainers.
summary.limitations: Editorial Design stands alone for article-like narratives and adds supporting styles only when a human annotation voice or data explanation is needed. Avoid handwritten body copy, dashboard-style chart walls, new chart fonts and unsourced numbers. Recomposition or pinning that hides hierarchy or crops key details should be adapted or omitted.
summary.assetRequirements: Use only supplied or authorized photographs and illustrations; do not assume photographic assets exist. Crops must fit grid proportions while keeping subjects, labels and attribution in frame. Serif and sans-serif font families are unspecified; measure and load them locally. Chart data must be supplied and sourced. Any PhotoSwipe gallery needs accurate image dimensions and responsive sources.
summary.combinations: Optional support styles: style-024 (margin notes) adds handwritten callouts in #A84235 marker ink, at most two per spread, placed in margins, never over body text, and drawn after their references. style-097 (infographic sidebars) sets charts within grid columns, with data in #252A30, accent only for highlighted series, and a caption and source line on each chart.
summary.productionApproach: HyperFrames is the primary render pipeline, using data-composition-id, a paused GSAP timeline in window.__timelines, then check, snapshot and render. Remotion is a documented fallback that requires a recorded reason. HTML/CSS and SVG are the style renderers; GSAP is the suggested motion engine, with Motion optional. chroma.js validates colors. PhotoSwipe, Cropper.js and Chartist are optional. Verify opening, action, transition and closing frames, text legibility and audio sync.
